Cascine (Parco delle Cascine) — Florence, Italy

🟡 Local press research

Average day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Parco delle Cascine, Florence's largest park, is one of the three areas under the Prefecture's official 'zona rossa' loitering-ban ordinance. It has a long, well-documented history of open-air drug dealing and street prostitution — including a Comune-led task force with the Prefecture specifically against prostitution and drug trafficking here, a 2020s investigation into an organised prostitution/trafficking ring, and a police officer stabbed/injured while arresting a dealer near the park's tram stop. By day the park's main avenues, sports facilities and river frontage are used normally by joggers, families and cyclists; the drug-dealing and prostitution activity is concentrated in specific wooded and tram-stop areas and is markedly worse after dark. Sources checked: FirenzeToday, Deputy Mayor Giachi on prostitution/drug-dealing task force at Cascine; FirenzeToday, drugs and prostitution at Cascine by night; La Nazione, police officer injured arresting dealer at Cascine tram stop; Controradio, Prefecture 'zone rosse' list including Parco delle Cascine.
